title: Failover orchestration conformance and snapshot bisect harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Build an automated conformance harness that validates active-passive failover orchestration end-to-end by exercising snapshot restore fidelity and using a bisect algorithm to find the first bad snapshot. The harness ties into SLO gates (latency/error rate), simulates circuit breaker trips and progressive load-shedding, and outputs a pass/fail signal for scheduled drills and pre-cutover checks.

Goals: 
- Provide deterministic validation that restore from snapshot (point-in-time) yields consistent KV/ledger state and application-level invariants across regions.
- Automate bisecting a range of snapshots to surface the earliest snapshot that fails validation (reduces manual forensic time).
- Integrate the harness with SLO checks so a drill is considered successful only if production SLOs remain within configured thresholds during stage transitions and traffic switch.
- Exercise circuit-breaker hysteresis and load-shedding policies during promotion to verify graceful degradation and no cascading service failure.

Success criteria (acceptance):
1) Harness can restore a snapshot set into an isolated ephemeral environment and run the standard verification suite (read-after-write checks, tokenstore integrity, KV checksum comparison, user-visible API smoke tests).
2) Bisect run returns a reproducible earliest-bad-snapshot identifier and preserved artifact links for forensic review.
3) During a scheduled drill run end-to-end, SLO regressions > 10% or errors > configured threshold trigger automatic rollback and produce a detailed incident artifact.
4) Circuit breaker/emergency-shedding simulation exercises at least 3 load profiles (normal, spike, sustained high) and validates fallback routing and partial-serving behavior.
5) Drill artifacts (dashboards, logs, snapshot manifests) are uploaded to the DR Confluence page and linked PRs/issues are created for any failures.

Runbook outline (for operator/drill lead):
- Preconditions: verify snapshot retention, ensure encryption keys/KMS access for ephemeral restores, disable scheduled production heavy jobs for drill window, notify stakeholders (SRE, Product, Support).
- Step 1 (Snapshot capture): capture production snapshot range [T0..Tn], tag with drill-id and metadata.
- Step 2 (Ephemeral restore & smoke): restore Tn into ephemeral VPC in the target region, run smoke suite and tokenstore integrity checks.
- Step 3 (Bisect): if smoke fails, run automated bisect which restores midpoints, runs verification suite, and narrows to earliest failing snapshot. Save diffs and checksums.
- Step 4 (Failover choreography): initiate passive promotion in canary mode (traffic siphon of low-volume customers), assert canary SLOs, expand to higher tiers if stable.
- Step 5 (Circuit breaker & load-shed injection): inject synthetic latency/errors and step up traffic to validate circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shed algorithms. Observe that degraded traffic is routed to fallback model variants or reduced-response modes per policy.
- Step 6 (Verification & backfill): after promotion, run read-after-write and end-to-end checks; if discrepancies, trigger rollback and create forensic artifacts.
- Step 7 (Postmortem & cleanup): upload artifacts, create tickets for fixes, rotate ephemeral infra and revoke access keys.

Technical design notes: 
- Bisector service: lightweight controller that drives RestoreJob CRs to ephemeral infra (k8s/ephemeral GPU if model state required), runs the verification harness, and records PASS/FAIL with standardized artifact URIs. Implement exponential backoff for noisy failures.
- Deterministic verification: suite includes checksums for critical TOKENS/LEDGER keys, a sampled end-to-end prompt/response corpus (stored in S3), and schema validation for persisted artifacts.
- Telemetry gating: integrate with Console SLO dashboards; harness will fail a drill if token-level latency or 5xx rates are above configured warn/error thresholds. Output a JSON artifact summarizing SLO deltas.
- Circuit breaker simulation: use the chaos injector to synthesize downstream latency and error rates, validate CB hysteresis and recovery windows.

Trade-offs and constraints: 
- Cost: frequent full bisect runs are expensive; initial rollout will run full bisect weekly for critical regions and monthly for others. Consider sampling strategy for long snapshot histories.
- Data privacy: restores use a scrubbed dataset unless a signed exception is provided. Scrubbing rules documented on Confluence.
- Restore time: long restores can delay bisect runs; implement incremental warmups and snapshot layering to speed tests.

Dependencies: 
- Snapshot retention policy update (PM work item) to keep minimum 30 days for bisecting.
- KMS/Key access for ephemeral restores (security).
- CI integration to allow scheduled runs and on-demand pre-cutover gating.

Artifacts & links: 
- Confluence design (DR/Bisector): https://confluence.redwood/example/dr-bisect-design (placeholder)
- Initial GH prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dr-bisector/pull/12
- Console SLO dashboard: https://console.redwood/slo/drill-dashboard

Acceptance tests: 
- Manual run by SRE team to validate end-to-end flow and bisect accuracy against known seeded corruption.
- Automated nightly smoke of harness that restores most recent snapshot and runs the verification suite.

Rollout plan: 
Phase 1 (2 weeks): deliver bisector prototype, wire up verification suite, run intra-team drills.
Phase 2 (4 weeks): integrate SLO gating and circuit-breaker simulation, run cross-team scheduled drill with product/ops observer.
Phase 3 (ongoing): enable weekly scheduled bisects for critical regions and incorporate into pre-cutover gating for major infra changes.

2026-03-11 - Liam Chen: Architecture review feedback - prefer ephemeral k8s namespaces over spinning full VM fleet to reduce cost. Suggested adding staged warmup to reduce restore time. See GH PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dr-bisector/pull/12

2026-03-11 - QA: Ran initial bisect against seeded corruption dataset. Bisector located failing snapshot T-47 in 4 restore iterations. Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-dr-artifacts/ENG-248105/2026-03-11/
2026-03-12 - Security (Marta Ruiz): Approved scrubbed-restore flow for test runs; real PII requires signed exception. Added KMS access checklist to Confluence page.

2026-03-12 - SRE (proposal): For canary promotion, use low-traffic customer cohort with circuit-breaker monitoring turned to 'alert' mode before full cutover. Need to schedule a 2-hour maintenance window for first cross-region drill.
